October 16, 2026

Three children and an adult killed in Oregon elementary school shooting

tags: policing, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

A shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday afternoon left three children and one adult dead, along with the suspected gunman. Authorities said a five-year-old, an eight-year-old and an 11-year-old were killed, while a seven-year-old child and a teacher were critically injured. The suspect, described by local authorities as a 16-year-old, was shot and killed by a bystander and had used a pump-action shotgun purchased by his mother. The FBI is assisting local police, and Bend-La Pine Schools canceled Friday classes and activities across its 33 schools.

Reuters reports White House ordered slowdown of Starshield access for Ukraine

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Reuters has reported that a White House official instructed the Department of Defense to slow down access to Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink used by the United States military and provided to Ukraine. Responsibility had previously been disputed between the White House, SpaceX and Elon Musk, who had pointed to the administration. Following the disruption, Russia launched one of its largest strikes since the 2022 invasion, with multiple fatalities and injuries and more than 600,000 people left without power. The White House said the president was not responsible but declined to comment on anyone else.

Pentagon prepares options for using MOAB against Iran

tags: war, defence
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

The US military has developed strike plans that include deploying the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast, the largest non-nuclear bomb in the American arsenal, against Iran. According to CNN and CBS News, potential targets include Iranian energy infrastructure and military and nuclear-related sites, though the 21,600-pound weapon is not designed to penetrate deeply buried facilities. The bomb was first used in combat against ISIS in Afghanistan in 2017. No order to use it has been announced.

Trump says he may have gone too far in striking Iranian leadership

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

President Trump said that successive waves of strikes on Iran's leadership had removed first-, second- and much of the third-level leadership, leaving him unsure who remained to negotiate with. He said he "might have gone too far" and that nobody wanted to serve as president of the Islamic Republic. He added that the situation was "going to end very soon." Critics noted that the Iranian government has survived and still controls the Strait of Hormuz.

FBI seizes Rep. Ilhan Omar's phone in immigration fraud investigation

tags: legal, politics, immigration
sources: @groundnews

Federal investigators have seized Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar's phone and issued more than a dozen grand jury subpoenas, including to her relatives, as part of a criminal investigation into potential immigration fraud, according to the Associated Press. Agents searched Omar's Washington, D.C., home on Monday, three weeks before the November midterm elections. US Attorney Jeanine Pirro said authorities are also examining Omar's financial disclosures. Omar denied the allegations and accused the administration of political intimidation, while Democrats criticized the timing of the search.

FBI investigates suspicious powder sent to election offices in multiple states

tags: politics, policing
sources: @total.hypocrisy

The FBI is investigating letters containing suspicious substances mailed to congressional offices and election offices. Packages containing a powdery substance led to the evacuation of election offices in Louisiana and Oklahoma this week, and the Ohio Secretary of State said the Postal Service intercepted a package containing white powder addressed to its office, with similar mailings sent to officials in several states. The incidents follow repeated instances of the president and his administration invoking national security justifications, including Trump declining on multiple occasions to rule out declaring a national emergency before or on election day.

Justice Department sues California over alleged non-citizen voter registrations

tags: legal, politics
sources: @total.hypocrisy

The Department of Justice announced it is suing the state of California over its determination that more than 20,000 likely non-citizens are registered to vote there. State voter registration processes compare records to verify citizenship when applications are submitted. The suit comes weeks ahead of the November midterm elections.

Matt Gaetz hit with federal sex trafficking lawsuit

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Former Congressman Matt Gaetz, President Trump's initial pick for attorney general, has been named in a new federal sex trafficking lawsuit filed in the Middle District of Florida. The 30-plus-page complaint alleges he participated in a scheme involving drugs, secret payments and luxury trips, and that he paid $400 to a 17-year-old girl for sex. Gaetz was previously under investigation by the Justice Department, and his nomination as attorney general did not proceed. He denies the allegations.

US trafficking ambassador tours Europe as administration blocks Epstein files

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Barbara Thornhill, the administration's new ambassador for human trafficking, met with Callista Gingrich, the ambassador to Switzerland, in what appears to be Thornhill's first overseas trip in the role. The visit comes as the administration continues to block European prosecutors from receiving key Epstein-related files, affecting investigations from Poland and Norway to France and the United Kingdom. The ambassadorship is responsible for combating trafficking in persons.

FBI director's Moscow trip questioned ahead of midterms

tags: politics, surveillance, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Reports that FBI Director Kash Patel had traveled to Moscow to meet FSB head Alexander Bortnikov were corrected after flight logs showed Patel was in Virginia, though the trip is described as long in the works and Democrats in Congress have called for it to be canceled. Bortnikov, FSB director since 2008, has been sanctioned by the United States twice, once over the poisoning of Alexei Navalny and once over election influence operations. In July 2026, the NSA, CISA, the FBI and partners from 12 countries issued a joint advisory attributing a decade-long router hacking campaign to FSB Center 16. Patel, Homeland Security Secretary Mark Wayne Mullin and Attorney General Todd Blanche have all declined under oath to rule out posting armed federal agents at polling places during the midterms.

White House press secretary faces mounting questions over resume and past work

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

Press Secretary Katie Zachariah is under scrutiny after reporting that she held herself out as an attorney despite failing the California bar exam. The New York Times spoke with the Zhong Lun law firm in China, where Shanghai-based partner Gary Gao said the firm often hires foreigners for language help and cultural guidance, confirming she never practiced Chinese law and that her role was closer to a paid intern than the associate title on her resume. Wired separately confirmed she promoted products for the company Beachbody in the early 2010s, which she described as "sort of a pyramid scheme." Republicans have raised calls for her removal following an appearance on Sean Hannity's show in which she was pressed on taking only three questions in 14 minutes.

Trump reportedly weighing replacement of chief of staff Susie Wiles

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump reportedly blew up overnight over negative headlines about White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, after aide Natalie Harp printed out copies of critical articles about her. According to Playbook, the White House is in a state of panic, with Wiles soliciting allies to speak favorably about her and her team. Potential replacements under discussion include DNI Jay Clayton, Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and a New York Yankees executive.

Trump says those who leak military plans should be shot

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

At an October 14 rally in Arizona, President Trump said people who leak sensitive US military plans "should be shot." He claimed that operational details involving US B-2 strikes on Iran had been leaked to the media. He announced no new policy on the matter.

Trump invokes executive privilege over Kennedy Center renovation talks

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

President Trump has claimed executive privilege to keep conversations about the Kennedy Center renovation secret, a claim that would also cover discussions held with non-government officials. Executive privilege bars other branches of government from accessing certain communications. The move follows earlier administration assertions of plenary authority, including Stephen Miller's claim on CNN that the president holds plenary authority under Title 10 in connection with federalizing the California National Guard.

Prosecutors weigh charges after ICE vehicle strikes Houston construction worker

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @groundnews

Miguel Parra Hernandez, a 48-year-old Mexican construction worker, remains hospitalized in ICE custody after an immigration officer struck him with an unmarked SUV during an enforcement operation in Houston. He underwent surgery for a broken leg and requires further ankle surgery. Surveillance footage shows the vehicle crossing a median and steering toward Hernandez as he fled through a parking lot; ICE says he ran in front of the vehicle during an operation targeting Jose Mendoza-Cervantes. Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare said the officer appeared to strike Hernandez intentionally and fled the scene, and prosecutors are considering criminal charges.

Anthropic warns self-replicating AI worms could spread across smart devices

tags: tech, surveillance
sources: @groundnews

Anthropic has warned that small AI models could become capable of spreading as self-replicating worms across internet-connected devices, including smart TVs and appliances, without human assistance by the end of 2026. Researchers demonstrated that a 26-billion-parameter model could run across 15 inexpensive Android TV boxes, and that a 9B model got inference running on eight of nine hardware types tested; in tests with reduced security barriers, a larger model spread across eight simulated devices. The company said such systems would be difficult to shut down because they lack a central point of control and can adapt to unfamiliar hardware, though replication would be slow, with a doubling time measured in days. Researchers recommended stronger device security and network monitoring.

Brazil's Senate votes 75-1 to end the six-day workweek

tags: politics, economy
sources: @groundnews

Brazil's Senate approved a constitutional amendment replacing the traditional six-day workweek with a five-day week, ahead of the October 25 presidential runoff between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and opposition candidate Flávio Bolsonaro. The reform phases in a 40-hour weekly limit without reducing pay and guarantees workers two paid days off, with employers determining which days. Congress is scheduled to enact the amendment Tuesday. Backed by more than 70% of Brazilians in polls, the measure became central to Lula's re-election campaign; Bolsonaro initially opposed it before reversing and pledging business tax relief.

Georgia sets record for first-day midterm early voting

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

Georgia recorded its highest first-day early voting turnout for a midterm election on Tuesday, with 188,667 in-person ballots cast, according to Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger's office. That is a 40% increase over the 134,962 votes cast on opening day in 2022 and well above the 70,849 cast in 2018. The state also accepted 10,267 absentee ballots. The November 3 election includes a Senate race between Democrat Jon Ossoff and Republican Mike Collins and a governor's race between Keisha Lance Bottoms and Rick Jackson.

Maduro returns to US federal court on torture charges

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro appeared in US federal court Thursday over new charges involving the alleged torture of Americans and political opponents.

Army chief warned missile defense stockpiles could stay low through 2030

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Former Army Chief Gen. Randy George reportedly warned the Pentagon that shortages of Patriot and THAAD missile-defense interceptors could persist until 2030. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth removed George from his post in April during the Iran war. No evidence establishes that the warning caused his removal.

Florida National Guard reports equipment readiness at 27%

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Florida National Guard leaders say mounting mission demands are stretching the force beyond its capacity. A maintenance review cut the force's reported equipment readiness from 90% to 27%.

Army to build some new barracks with 25-year lifespans

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Army plans to construct some new barracks designed to last 25 years rather than the traditional 50-year standard. The change follows the relocation of nearly 5,200 military medical trainees from failing modular dormitories built in 2014.

Army creates nationwide HVAC task force after Fort Carson barracks failures

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Soldiers at Fort Carson reported sleeping in their cars after barracks temperatures climbed into the 90s. The Army has established its first nationwide heating and air conditioning task force and directed $15 million toward 44 priority repair projects.

Administration finalizes rule allowing bear baiting on Alaska preserves

tags: environment, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The administration has finalized a rule, scheduled for publication on October 19, that reverses wildlife protections for bears on Alaska's national preserves. The rule permits hunters to use human food, including donuts and bacon grease, as bait to lure bears in and then shoot them at close range. The foods used as bait are harmful to the animals.

Scorecard tallies 37 broken MAHA promises and none kept

tags: health, politics, environment
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A tracking project scoring the administration against its Make America Healthy Again commitments counts 37 broken promises and none kept. Items cited include the appointment of a former pesticide lobbyist to oversee pesticide regulation and the USDA's cancellation of more than $660 million in local food for schools programs. The scorecard also notes nearly $2 billion in EPA clean air and water funding cut.

England and Wales to ban pornography depicting strangulation and incest

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

England and Wales will ban pornography depicting strangulation, incest or adults pretending to be children under 16, starting November 6, with possession or distribution becoming a criminal offense. The legislation follows a 2025 government-commissioned review that found depictions of choking were "rife" on pornography websites and were normalizing the practice among young people. Conservative peer Baroness Gabby Bertin, who led the review, said the law sends an unequivocal signal that violent sexual content is unacceptable. Justice minister Alex Davies-Jones urged those holding prohibited material to delete it.
